content: Cefazolin contains ingredients that may trigger allergic reactions or other complications. It can reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication is known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of severe side effects. It is essential to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefazolin may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as the Coombs' test or specific urine glucose tests, potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your healthcare provider. While using this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as a complete blood count or kidney function tests, to monitor your progress and check for side effects. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not attempt to double the dose to make up for the missed one. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or suitable for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common side effects of cefazolin may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, it may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. In rare cases, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterium called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. For any concerns about side effects, U.S. residents should contact their doctor, and Canadian residents should do the same. Always follow your healthcare provider's instructions and ask for clarification if needed.
